aboutPage.evccCredit: Wallboxes are controlled by {link}, an independent open source project. OpenAmpere uses its open interface. Thanks to the evcc community!
aboutPage.foxessCredit: FoxESS register definitions are based on foxess_modbus (MIT License).
aboutPage.intro: OpenAmpere is an independent community project for solar systems with battery storage. It runs entirely locally and needs no cloud.
aboutPage.license: OpenAmpere is free software under the MIT License.
aboutPage.selfHosted: You run this installation yourself on your own computer. OpenAmpere does not send any data to the project.
aboutPage.trademarks: All product names and brands mentioned belong to their respective owners. Legal notes and background: see the README in the source code.

appearancePage.languageHint: Applies to this device only. English is not complete yet, missing texts appear in German. Translations are welcome.
appearancePage.themeHint: “Automatic” follows the setting of your device. Applies to this device only.
appearancePage.timeZoneHint: Days, times and daily values follow it, even when you open the app abroad.

appsPage.codeShownOnce: The code is only shown now. It works like a key: do not share it, only paste it into the app.
appsPage.controlScopeHint: The app may also change the work mode, battery limits, charging from the grid and the mode of your devices – only while control is turned on here. The main switch, export limit and settings stay with OpenAmpere.
appsPage.haCodeHint: In Home Assistant: Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → OpenAmpere, then paste the code.
appsPage.httpsError: HTTPS for other apps is not available: {error}. Another program is using the port. To fix it, set OPENAMPERE_SERVER_TLS_PORT in docker-compose.yml to a free port, e.g. “8444”, and restart OpenAmpere.
appsPage.httpsOff: The HTTPS port is turned off (server.tls_port = 0). Without it, other apps cannot connect securely.
appsPage.intro: Other apps such as Home Assistant can read the data of OpenAmpere and, if you allow it, control the battery. Each app gets its own access, which you can remove at any time. The connection is encrypted.
appsPage.pairingHint: The easiest way: in Home Assistant, add the OpenAmpere integration and choose “Pair with OpenAmpere”. The request then appears here. Alternatively, create an access here and paste the connection code:
appsPage.readScopeHint: The app sees power, energy, state of charge and status, but cannot change anything.
appsPage.removeText: “{name}” will no longer be able to access OpenAmpere. For a new connection, create a new access.

batteryPage.backupLowerLimitHint: During a power cut, the battery is discharged down to this level and no further. At most as high as the backup reserve.
batteryPage.backupReserveHint: This much always stays in the battery in everyday use, so there is energy during a power cut.
batteryPage.maxSocHint: The battery is charged up to this value.
batteryPage.overwritten: Another device (e.g. the previous Smartbox) overwrote your change shortly afterwards: {changes}.
batteryPage.overwrittenHint: As long as it is connected, these values cannot be changed permanently.
batteryPage.readOnly: Display only – OpenAmpere cannot change settings on {manufacturer} devices yet.
batteryPage.smartboxHint: A previous Smartbox regularly fetches its settings from the cloud. If you block its internet access in your router, your changes will stay.
batteryPage.testModeLogged: Test mode: the change was only logged
batteryPage.title: Battery & backup power
batteryPage.unreadValues: Some values could not be read just now ({values}). They are shown as “?”; the limits can only be changed once all values have been read.

chargingPage.acceptRegistration: I have read this and will take care of the registration myself.
chargingPage.capacityHint: From the datasheet, used to calculate the charging time.
chargingPage.cheapestHint: Finds the cheapest quarter hours up to this time. Needs a dynamic or time-of-use tariff.
chargingPage.eegWarning: If the battery charges from the grid, this can affect the EEG compensation for electricity later fed in from the battery (exclusivity principle). Since 2025 there are separation and flat-rate rules for this, which must be registered with the grid operator. A battery with more than 4.2 kW of grid charging power may also fall under § 14a EnWG.
chargingPage.intro: Charges the battery from the grid when electricity is cheap or in a fixed time window (e.g. night tariff).
chargingPage.maxChargingPower: Permitted charging power of the battery
chargingPage.maxPowerHint: According to the datasheet; small batteries often allow less than the inverter can do, e.g. 5.5 kW for 6.6 kWh. Leave empty if unknown.
chargingPage.maxPriceHint: Never charges above this price, even if the target is not reached.
chargingPage.powerLevels: Gentle {gentle} kW, fast {fast} kW, maximum {max} kW: 50, 75 and 100 % of the permitted charging power.
chargingPage.powerTooHigh: The charging power is set higher than the battery allows. Please choose a level.
chargingPage.registrationHint: OpenAmpere only charges and never discharges into the grid. Clarify the registration with your grid operator or tax advisor before you use this feature.
chargingPage.remoteControlHint: For this, OpenAmpere uses the inverter's remote control with a time limit: if OpenAmpere stops, the inverter returns to normal operation by itself after 3 minutes. For “Cheapest time” you need a dynamic or time-of-use electricity tariff.
chargingPage.section14aHint: Above 4.2 kW of charging power from the grid, the battery may fall under § 14a EnWG (controllable consumers). Check this with your grid operator.
chargingPage.targetHint: State of charge at which charging from the grid stops.
chargingPage.title: Charging from the grid
chargingPage.turnOnTitle: Turn on charging from the grid?

cloudImportCard.disclaimer: OpenAmpere is an independent project and has nothing to do with Energiekonzepte Deutschland GmbH (EKD). It was neither commissioned nor authorized by EKD. The import only uses the customer API of the EKD cloud with your personal key. “EKD” and “Ampere.IQ” are names belonging to their owners.
cloudImportCard.durationHint: The EKD cloud only allows about one request per minute, so the import takes a few hours (around 2 minutes per day). It keeps running in the background, even if you close the app or restart OpenAmpere. OpenAmpere's own readings are never overwritten.
cloudImportCard.exportFileHint: Already saved your history with the export tool? Then choose the export folder as a ZIP file here.
cloudImportCard.findingStart: Looking for the start of your records …
cloudImportCard.imported: {count} quarter hours of energy values imported
cloudImportCard.independent: OpenAmpere is independent and has nothing to do with EKD.
cloudImportCard.intro: Import your history from the “Ampere.IQ” app while the EKD cloud is still available. You'll find the key in the Ampere.IQ app under {menu}.
cloudImportCard.keyHint: Only stored on this server and never shown again.
cloudImportCard.saveKeyFirst: Save the API key first to start.
cloudImportCard.stepBattery: Step 2 of 2: battery state of charge, {done} of {total} days
cloudImportCard.stepEnergy: Step 1 of 2: energy values, {done} of {total} days
cloudImportCard.title: History from the EKD cloud

connectionPage.checkConnection: Check or set up the connection
connectionPage.expertHint: Only change this if automatic detection gets it wrong. Saving reconnects.
connectionPage.foxessNewer: FoxESS H3 – newer firmware / Smart / Pro
connectionPage.gridMeterHint: Smart meter readings from the customer portal
connectionPage.newIpFound: The inverter had a new IP address and was found again automatically ({when}, {from} → {to}). Tip: give it a fixed address in your router.
connectionPage.perPollHint: OpenAmpere connects anew for every poll and releases access afterwards – for devices that another energy manager is also connected to.
connectionPage.permanentHint: A permanent connection is the fastest. If another energy manager (e.g. the Smartbox) keeps losing its connection, choose “Per poll”.
connectionPage.pollHint: How often the inverter is polled. 10 seconds is a good value.
connectionPage.timeoutHint: If the inverter is behind a Modbus proxy or on Wi-Fi, a higher value can prevent dropped connections.

connectionStatus.addIntegrationStep: Add the integration and choose “Pair with OpenAmpere”: {link}. Enter there:
connectionStatus.allowStep: The request then appears at the top of this page with a code. If it matches the one in Home Assistant, allow it.
connectionStatus.checkAddress: Can Home Assistant reach this address? The integration must use {host} with HTTPS port {port} in its settings.
connectionStatus.checkRunning: Is Home Assistant running, and is the OpenAmpere integration set up there?
connectionStatus.installHacsStep: In Home Assistant, install {link} if you haven't already.
connectionStatus.installIntegrationStep: Install the OpenAmpere integration through HACS and restart Home Assistant:
connectionStatus.intro: This shows the values of OpenAmpere in Home Assistant, including the energy dashboard, and lets you control the battery from there if you like. OpenAmpere is already running, only the integration is missing.
connectionStatus.manualHint: Without HACS or for other apps: create an access below and paste the connection code. The address must be the one at which Home Assistant reaches this computer, usually the IP address.
connectionStatus.notConnected: No app is connected right now.
connectionStatus.notConnectedSince: No app is connected right now, last at {date}.
connectionStatus.reconnectHint: Does Home Assistant show “Reconnect”? Then the access was removed here or the certificate has changed: simply pair again.
connectionStatus.title: Connect Home Assistant

controlPage.overwriteHint: As long as another energy manager (e.g. the previous Smartbox) is connected, it can overwrite settings again. After making changes, check that they stay.

csvExportCard.hint: Energy values as a CSV file, e.g. for Excel, Numbers or your tax return.
csvExportCard.title: Export as a spreadsheet

dataPage.backupHint: Downloads the complete database with all readings and settings. Keep the file in a safe place. Passwords and API keys are not included.
dataPage.retentionHint: Readings every few seconds for the power curve. Quarter-hourly and daily values are always kept.

diagnosticsPage.checkAfterChange: After the first change in live mode, check in “My system” and in the log that the value is kept.
diagnosticsPage.checkHint: Items marked “Check” explain below what they mean. Often values are scaled wrongly or missing; a shared report helps to fix that for your device.
diagnosticsPage.copyFailed: Copying did not work. Please select the report below and copy it.
diagnosticsPage.explanation: The diagnostics read all register blocks, check scaling and the export limit, and look at how the device behaves at night and when the daily counters reset. You can share the report so that more devices get supported.
diagnosticsPage.fullSerial: Include the full serial number in the report
diagnosticsPage.gridOperatorQuestions: Which export limit applies (commissioning date, kWp, smart meter)? Is control under § 9 EEG or § 14a EnWG handled by the Smartbox or a control box?
diagnosticsPage.intro: Checks whether OpenAmpere understands your inverter correctly.
diagnosticsPage.otherDevicesHint: Note the manufacturer and model and mention them in an issue – this decides whether and how OpenAmpere can support it.
diagnosticsPage.readOnly: It only reads, nothing is changed.
diagnosticsPage.shareHint: Help others with the same device: copy the report and paste it into an issue on GitHub.
diagnosticsPage.takesHalfMinute: This takes about half a minute …
diagnosticsPage.testConnections: Also test how many connections work at the same time (may briefly disturb other devices such as the Smartbox)

downloadButton.shareFailed: The file could not be shared.

eegCard.differentHint: If your grid operator's statement differs, switch off the automatic calculation and enter the value for the tariff.
eegCard.intro: OpenAmpere calculates the rate from the commissioning date, PV capacity and type of feed-in, just like the grid operator. Otherwise the value you enter for the tariff applies.
eegCard.period: Applies to systems commissioned from {from} to {to}.
eegCard.periodWithoutFullFeedIn: Applies to systems commissioned from {from} to {to}, back then without a separate rate for full feed-in.
eegCard.rate: {rate} for every kilowatt hour fed in
eegCard.tiers: The power is split across the tiers (§ 23c EEG): {tiers}.
eegCard.title: Feed-in tariff
eegCard.typeHint: Surplus: you use solar power yourself and only feed in the rest (the usual case with a battery). Full feed-in: everything goes to the grid, which has earned higher rates since 30 July 2022.
eegCard.whereToFind: You'll find both on the grid operator's first statement or in the Marktstammdatenregister.

events.alarmHint: When the inverter reports a fault code.
events.batteryFullHint: Once a day, a good moment for large appliances.
events.batteryHealthHint: Battery cells very warm or unusually different in temperature.
events.cheapPowerHint: Only with a dynamic tariff, as soon as tomorrow's prices are available.
events.firmwareHint: The inverter reports a different firmware, for example after an update.
events.offGridHint: When the house runs on backup power and when the grid is back.
events.overwrittenHint: When another device reverts a change made by OpenAmpere.
events.unreachableHint: After 15 minutes without a connection, and when it is back.

exportLimitPage.aboveRule: The current value is higher than the chosen rule allows ({max}).
exportLimitPage.confirmConsent: You confirm that you have your grid operator's written consent ({reference}).
exportLimitPage.consentCheckbox: I have the {consent} for this feed-in power.
exportLimitPage.consentNeeded: With a fixed value from the grid operator (or if you don't know the rule), this is only allowed with the grid operator's written consent. Depending on the grid operator, a registered electrician may also have to make or report the change.
exportLimitPage.consentReference: Date and reference of the consent
exportLimitPage.enterPvCapacity: Enter the PV capacity above so OpenAmpere can calculate the allowed value.
exportLimitPage.increasing: You are increasing the feed-in power.
exportLimitPage.legalHint: The limit comes from the law (e.g. 60 % of PV capacity under the Solarspitzengesetz) or from your grid connection approval. Violations can lead to payments under § 52 EEG. Usually the installer sets the limit.
exportLimitPage.notSupported: The export limit of this device cannot be read or changed via Modbus. Please contact a qualified electrician.
exportLimitPage.penaltyWarning: Feeding in more than allowed can mean payments to the grid operator.
exportLimitPage.referenceHint: Saved in the log together with the change.
exportLimitPage.responsibility: As the system operator, you are responsible for complying with the grid connection conditions.
exportLimitPage.smartboxHint: Check whether the limit used to be enforced by the Smartbox: in that case the inverter may be set to 100 %, and without the box only the value here applies.
exportLimitPage.testModeLogged: Test mode: the change was only logged
exportLimitPage.unchanged: That is already the current value.
exportLimitPage.writtenConsent: written consent of my grid operator

feedInRuleCard.declaration: I declare that {neither} limits feed-in for my system – for example because a smart metering system with a control box is installed.
feedInRuleCard.declarationLogged: The declaration is saved in the log.
feedInRuleCard.declareHint: You can then allow feed-in up to the inverter's power without being asked again.
feedInRuleCard.neitherLawNorGrid: neither the law nor the grid connection approval
feedInRuleCard.pvCapacityHint: The sum of all panels, e.g. from the Marktstammdatenregister or your invoice. The percentage rules refer to this, not to the inverter.
feedInRuleCard.title: Your system

feedInRules.limit60Hint: Solarspitzengesetz (solar peak law): commissioned from 25 February 2025, as long as no smart metering system with a control box is installed.
feedInRules.limit70Hint: Earlier rule. No longer applies to systems up to 25 kWp commissioned after 14 September 2022, or to older systems up to 7 kWp.
feedInRules.noneHint: Neither the law nor the grid connection approval limits feed-in.
feedInRules.operator: Fixed value from the grid operator
feedInRules.operatorHint: Stated in the grid connection approval, e.g. zero feed-in. Any increase needs the grid operator's written consent.
feedInRules.unknownHint: Ask your installer or grid operator. Until then, any increase needs the grid operator's written consent.

gridMeterPage.atLeastOneMeter: At least one meter must be counted.
gridMeterPage.credentialsHint: Your login details stay on your device and are only sent to {operator}. Fetching does not work with two-factor login.
gridMeterPage.credentialsHintGeneric: Your login details stay on your device and are only sent to the grid operator. Fetching does not work with two-factor login.
gridMeterPage.delayHint: The grid operator often provides a day only in the afternoon of the next day. OpenAmpere checks every three hours and only takes complete days. Until then, the inverter's values count.
gridMeterPage.intro: You are billed by your grid operator's meter. If you have a smart meter, the grid operator shows the daily values in its customer portal. OpenAmpere fetches them there and then compares your advance payments with these values instead of the inverter's.
gridMeterPage.metersHint: Choose the meters that belong to your house connection. A separate meter, e.g. for a heat pump, is billed separately.
gridMeterPage.moreOperatorsHint: Every grid operator has its own customer portal, so they are added one by one.
gridMeterPage.operatorHint: Shown on your electricity bill or on the meter.
gridMeterPage.regionHint: Grid area: {region}. Log in as in the customer portal {portal}.
gridMeterPage.savedKeep: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.

installationPage.faultCodes: The inverter reports a fault code: {codes}.
installationPage.faultHint: The manufacturer's manual explains what it means. Tell your installer the code if the message stays.

licensesPage.intro: OpenAmpere is free software under the MIT License and builds on these open source components. Thanks to everyone who develops them!

more.connectionHint: Inverter, immersion heater, wallbox, grid operator
more.dataHint: Backup, export, history from the EKD cloud
more.diagnosticsHint: Check the device and share a report

notifyPage.addressHint: Server and topic, e.g. https://ntfy.sh/a-long-random-word. Anyone who knows the topic can read along – so pick something that cannot be guessed.
notifyPage.advancedHint: Only needed for your own ntfy server or a topic you already have.
notifyPage.allSet: Great, everything is set up. Below you choose when OpenAmpere should get in touch.
notifyPage.androidSteps: Tap “Open in ntfy”. ntfy opens and subscribes to your topic by itself.
notifyPage.appStore: iPhone: ntfy on the App Store
notifyPage.computerSteps: On a computer? Scan the code with your phone's camera to get your topic's address onto the phone. Even easier: open this page (More → Notifications) on the phone itself, then there is nothing to type.
notifyPage.helpAllow: Allow ntfy to show notifications. iPhone: Settings → Notifications → ntfy → turn on “Allow Notifications”. Android: Settings → Apps → ntfy → turn on notifications.
notifyPage.helpBattery: Android: exclude ntfy from battery saving (Settings → Apps → ntfy → Battery → “Unrestricted”). The menu names differ a little between phones.
notifyPage.helpFocus: Check whether “Do Not Disturb” or a Focus is turned on. Then the phone shows no notifications. Open ntfy itself: if the test message is there, it arrives and only the alert is missing.
notifyPage.helpOwnServer: Own ntfy server: under {advanced}, the full address including the topic is needed, e.g. https://ntfy.example.org/my-topic, and the same server must be entered in ntfy when subscribing. For iPhones, the server also needs the upstream-base-url setting.
notifyPage.helpTopic: The topic in ntfy must be exactly: {topic}. Compare it character by character. If it differs, delete the topic in ntfy and set it up again as in step 2.
notifyPage.installText: Install the free app {app} on your phone. You don't need an account.
notifyPage.intro: Alerts on your phone with the free app {app} (iPhone and Android, no account needed).
notifyPage.invalidAddress: The saved address does not have the form https://server/topic. Correct it under {advanced} or delete it, then you can let a topic be suggested.
notifyPage.iosSteps: On the iPhone: tap {copy}. Then open ntfy, tap the plus sign, paste the topic into the field (long press → “Paste”) and confirm the subscription.
notifyPage.ownTopicHint: Already have a topic or your own ntfy server? Enter the address below under {advanced}.
notifyPage.privacyHint: On ntfy.sh, messages are briefly stored on someone else's server. If you don't want that, you can run your own ntfy server in your home network.
notifyPage.qrLabel: QR code with the address of your ntfy topic
notifyPage.savedKeep: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
notifyPage.testFirst: As soon as a topic is set up, you can send a test message here.
notifyPage.testText: Send yourself a test message. It should appear on your phone within a few seconds.
notifyPage.tokenHint: Only for protected topics on your own servers.
notifyPage.topicExplain: A topic is like a secret channel: only those who know its name receive the messages. OpenAmpere makes up a long, random name and saves it right away.
notifyPage.yourTopic: Your topic – it must have exactly this name in ntfy too:

pairingCard.checkCode: Only allow the connection if the app shows {code}. If it shows a different one, decline: someone may be trying to listen in.
pairingCard.title: “{name}” wants to connect

priceChart.chartLabel: Electricity price today per quarter hour
priceChart.noPrices: No exchange prices loaded for today yet (needs internet).
priceChart.title: Electricity price today

pvSystemPage.hiddenHint: Hidden inputs don't appear anywhere in the display or the report. OpenAmpere keeps storing their readings, and you can show them again at any time.
pvSystemPage.intro: Give your PV strings names like “South roof” or “Garage”. The current power helps you tell them apart. If the inverter reports an input with nothing connected to it, hide it.
pvSystemPage.noInputs: No PV inputs detected yet. In the dark the inputs have no voltage – check again during the day.

remotePage.about: Tailscale (Tailscale Inc., USA) sets up the connection between your devices. The data itself travels encrypted directly between your phone and this computer. This way OpenAmpere can only be reached by devices logged in to your Tailscale account. Tailscale is free for personal use.
remotePage.accountStep: Log in to Tailscale or create an account.
remotePage.appStep: Install the Tailscale app on your phone and log in with the same account.
remotePage.approvalNeeded: Your Tailscale account requires new devices to be approved. Approve “{name}” in the {link} to continue.
remotePage.continuesAutomatically: This page continues by itself afterwards.
remotePage.disconnectText: OpenAmpere can then only be reached at home. You can set it up again at any time.
remotePage.homeHint: At home, the usual address keeps working. On an iPhone only one VPN can be on at a time.
remotePage.homeScreenStep: Open the address above in the browser and add it to your home screen.
remotePage.httpsEnable: HTTPS is not enabled in your Tailscale account yet. Open the link, confirm there and come back – it continues by itself.
remotePage.httpsFailed: HTTPS could not be switched on. Is “HTTPS Certificates” on in the Tailscale account? Message: {error}
remotePage.httpsHint: With HTTPS the browser shows the lock and the address needs no port. For this, “HTTPS Certificates” must be enabled under {link} in your Tailscale account. The name of this device is then listed in a public directory of certificates; the app itself stays private.
remotePage.httpsOn: HTTPS is on. The address above now starts with https://.
remotePage.installScriptHint: After that, one tap here is enough. Installed manually? See the {link}.
remotePage.intro: With Tailscale you can reach OpenAmpere securely from anywhere, without any port forwarding in your router. Tailscale connects your devices directly and encrypted. You need a free Tailscale account; you can sign in with Google, Apple or Microsoft, for example.
remotePage.logInHint: Now log in to Tailscale. If you don't have an account yet, create one there.
remotePage.logInStep: Log in with the same account and turn Tailscale on.
remotePage.logInStepAccount: Log in with the same account ({account}) and turn Tailscale on.
remotePage.noLoginLink: Tailscale did not provide a login link. Check the internet connection of this computer and try again.
remotePage.notInstalled: Tailscale is not set up on this computer yet. To set it up, run the install script once more:
remotePage.offlineHint: In your {link} the device stays listed as “offline”. You can delete it there if you no longer want to use Tailscale.
remotePage.phoneTitle: How to use it on your phone
remotePage.privacy: OpenAmpere turns off sending log data to Tailscale and exposes nothing publicly to the internet. Changing settings remotely also requires your password.

storageHint.growth: Without a limit, it grows by about {size} per year.
storageHint.needed: OpenAmpere needs about {size} for {period} of detailed data.
storageHint.sizeAndFree: The database is now {size}, with {free} still free.

tariffPage.exchangePriceHint: Exchange prices come free of charge from aWATTar (day-ahead market). The server needs internet access for this.
tariffPage.feedInHint: What you receive per kilowatt hour fed in. You'll find it on your grid operator's statement.
tariffPage.intro: OpenAmpere uses this to calculate savings, electricity costs and the comparison with your advance payments (Report). If you change tariff, add a new one with a start date. OpenAmpere keeps calculating earlier periods with the old price.
tariffPage.priceHint: What you pay per kilowatt hour from the grid.
tariffPage.standingChargeHint: A fixed amount per month, regardless of consumption. You'll find it in your contract.
tariffPage.surchargeHint: Everything added to the exchange price: grid fees, levies, taxes, margin. You'll find it in your contract or on your bill.

timeWindows.hint: Times with their own price, e.g. a night tariff from 00:30 to 05:30 or the time windows of time-variable grid fees. A window may span midnight.

workModes.backupHint: The battery is only charged and kept full for power cuts.
workModes.feedInFirstHint: Surplus goes to the grid first, the battery is not discharged.
workModes.peakShavingHint: The battery only covers high consumption peaks.
workModes.selfUseHint: Use solar power in the house first and store the surplus. Recommended.
